implementation_notes: Default Node realization where the log is the broker: the group id is the durable subscription identity and committed offsets are the retained position. Choose it when Node services consume an existing Kafka topic and the catch-up window should follow the topic's retention.
pitfalls: eachMessage auto-commits after resolution, so a crash mid-batch replays the batch - deduplicate.
A slow handler exceeding sessionTimeout is removed from the group and its partitions are reassigned mid-batch.

variants.name: MQTT persistent session (mqtt.js clean:false)
variants.implementation_notes: Where MQTT is the transport, the broker stores the session for the clientId and queues QoS 1/2 publications while the client is offline. Choose it for device or edge consumers; the same client id must be reused, and the library can only tell you the session survived via connack.sessionPresent.
pitfalls: A generated or rotated client id silently creates a fresh session, discarding the queued backlog.
Session expiry is negotiated with the broker: MQTT 5 clients must set a session expiry interval or the session ends at disconnect.
